Cautious-hold message confirmed, with SLOOS tilting the balance more defensively. The FOMC kept the target range at 5.25–5.50 percent, reiterated “greater confidence” is needed before cutting, and maintained QT caps ($25B Treasuries, $35B agency MBS) and standing repo/RRP settings to anchor short rates. While the statement notes solid activity and continued disinflation progress, the latest Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey indicates credit headwinds that temper the macro tone: banks, on net, reported tight lending standards and soft demand across key categories—C&I (large and middle‑market firms), CRE (notably office), residential real estate, and consumer credit (credit cards, auto, other). Elevated spreads and stricter terms imply restrictive credit supply, which can weigh on growth and help cool inflation, but also raise downside risks. Together with financial‑stability vulnerabilities (CRE, nonbank leverage, liquidity under stress), the SLOOS results reinforce a risk‑management stance and a high bar for near‑term easing.

Net effect versus a pure macro read: slightly more guarded. Adjusting for SLOOS, the tone shifts from modestly positive to only mildly positive.
